claims.claim: Reviewers describe the dialogue and voice writing as simplistic, uninspired, or feeling like it was written for children.

citations.review_text: So far not good, story is okay, combat is fine I guess but no challenge at all other chapters you had to struggle from beginning, but whose genius idea was to put 2 archers and one mage, so if i picked archer it would be three archers in a squad. Graphics are not good, everything has some sort of filter, game doesn't look good at all, especially compared to other games in 2026. The worst part for me is dialogues, it is like it was written by a literal child. you press button and they tell you something opened downstairs, no ♥♥♥♥ lady I literally see the door that opened. You wouldn't want people to talk to you like this in real life, so why would I want it in video game. Characters have nothing to say, but authors force them to just say random stuff, sometimes it is better not to talk at all. All characters are ugly and for some reason have giant heads!! I picked one character in character creation and he looked completely different in a game.

I wanted to really give this game a try, but it was really unbearable to get through. These games are meant to be heavily narrative-driven, and the voice writing for it is honestly pretty awful. It feels like it's written like a Disney movie plot but made to be "for older audiences" while making conversations even less inspired than that. I'd say this is written like someone's entry-level fanfic about Dragon Age more than it feels like a sequel to Inquisition. I'd recommend playing Inquisition instead and skipping this game entirely. I could only recommend this game if you want to play for the combat and enjoy skipping cutscenes, or you're not caring at all about the story, or you would simply enjoy having, not gonna lie, a pretty good character creator. 9 out of 10 thumbs down.

citations.review_text: Sound issues make this game unbearable. There is currently no fix(after 2 years) DO NOT BUY unless you know it's going to work for you.

First Impressions Review

I have been playing games my whole life, probably like most of you. I am also a D&D Dungeon Master, and as far as I remember, this is my first steam game review.

I have only been playing Dragon Age: The Veilguard for about an hour, but I already had to stop playing just to write this review and share my thoughts.

My computer is about eight years old, and somehow the game runs nicely. I had a few crashes, while I had dozens of tabs opened, but the game recovered from the exact moment it stopped, which honestly impressed me. And that is where the bad part ends.

This game is absolutely brilliant.

I love the story, the characters, the graphics, the combat, and the overall presentation. So far, this feels like the best RPG game I have ever played. It is also giving me so many amazing ideas for my D&D campaigns, which is always a sign that a game is doing something special.

The combat is fun and satisfying, but this is not Diablo. There is a real sense of story, character, and choice from the beginning. It feels like what you do matters, and that makes the experience much more engaging for me.

And yes, I already mentioned the graphics, but let me say it again: the presentation is incredible. The lip sync is on another level. The cutscenes are so well-made that it honestly blows my mind how many of them there are, especially with how naturally they are mixed with combat and exploration.

For the kind of RPG I enjoy, this game has the perfect balance: story, action, beautiful visuals, strong characters, and a world that immediately pulls me in.

So far, Dragon Age: The Veilguard is a truly enjoyable and fun experience.

10 out of 10.

Only played it a little bit but the game has some memory leak. Runs fine for the first 30 min and then perfomance dips. After restart it is fine again. I doubt this is only an issue with 6 gb VRAM cards like mine.

Found some workaround trough the MODloader thing but i think this is a massive issue for most casual gamers that want to try this out.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a linear level design with corridor-like exploration rather than open areas.

citations.review_text:
Had this on my wishlist and wanted to play it just to see how bad it really is, and lemme tell ya, it's BAD. 

If you briefly glimpse gameplay it looks competently made, but the flaws quickly rack up. 

The writing is insufferable, all quirky milennial sarcasm humour with cliché lines and questionable voice acting all over the place. 

The combat actually feels kinda fun but you have 3 abilities per character now instead of like 10, AND party size is reduced. 

Level design is back to Dragon Age 2 which might be the biggest crime. If you make a sequel you better make it just as good or better, not this massive downgrade to linear levels when we had beautiful big maps to explore in Inquisition. 

Gonna try to continue to see where it leads but I don't have high hopes.

Oh and I've played all Dragon Ages on keyboard and mouse so far because it's the best way to play them, but I'm playing this one with a controller. Why? Because they made controller good? No it's just as ♥♥♥♥ as it's always been for Dragon Age except this time they made Keyboard and Mouse even worse. I don't even know how you accomplish that.

I know I haven't made it especially far into the game but after 5 hours, I would expect my RPG to have opened up at least a bit. I'm not upset that it isn't another generic open-world RPG like so many have gone the route of but I would have hoped that the areas we are given to explore actually had a bit of exploration. At this point, it just feels like I am putting my brain on auto-pilot and walking in a practically straight line. The locations do not feel like a lived-in world with characters who add to the storytelling. It is just one long hallway after another. Every once in a while, there is a chest or something that you have to engage with the least amount of verticality to reach but most of the time it is just going from point A to point B unbroken and endlessly which feels crazy for a game series where we should have more freedom to explore than ever with the working eluvians.

I really want to enjoy this game. I mean that genuinely because Dragon Age: Origins has been my favorite game for most of my life. I have always at least been able to find some amount of good in the games going forward from that one. Awakening was a fun sort of semi-sequel that I appreciated for letting me step back into the shoes of my Grey Warden. Dragon Age 2 gave us an interesting update to the combat mechanics which I will admit felt somewhat dated in the original game. Inquisition opened up so much and made the world feel so much more alive now that we were able to explore the politics of Orlais and could even play a Qunari for the first time.

I hate to be so negative about one of my all-time favorite game series, especially when so much of the discourse is from people hating this game for having inclusive options for Rook and characters who add diversity to the cast. It sucks to have to pre-empt my issues with the game by saying that I do not agree with the bad faith actors who were never going to like this game, even if it was a perfect experience that made good on the bui…

IF you havnt played previous Dragon age games disregard half of this review.

I tried to give it a shot but unfortunately i cannot recommend this game at all.

should have been a separate game called veilguard, this is a mindless press X game where you dont have to buy potions they are just there and are refiled by breaking green urns, you cant change your party, you cant go solo without a party, there is zero exploration as it is entirely linear and the yellow paint syndrome along with having Navi like yelling in your ear "HEY GO THERE!" is way to handholdy, companions have infinite health, the merchants you have to level up like a survival game, enemies give the tiniest amount of XP making grinding levels only possibly through following the story, which is the only thing to do so grinding for levels is irrelevant as its just easy mode the whole game, the story is bland and just borrows enemy names from previous games without following any lore, the character creation is a joke, and is impossible to make a normal looking person without a chad face, its like they took the worst ports of inquisition and made them even worse. the class system is a joke, combat feels decent but its literally just harry potter. exploration/moving from point A to B is like a gutted version of god of war, i wouldn't recommend this game at all. it makes me sad.

I refunded the game even with a 70% discount.

The writing is the main reason I can't recommend this.

Veilguard feels weirdly childish for a game aimed at a mature audience. The story is supposedly about ancient elven gods threatening the world, but the dialogue often sounds like it belongs in a kids' adventure show. Characters joke, banter and explain their feelings in a way that completely clashes with the scale of what's happening. Instead of tension, dread or moral complexity, the game keeps giving you safe, overly polished dialogue that feels sanitised and immature.

That's the biggest mismatch. Dragon Age used to feel like dark fantasy, with politics, religion, betrayal, racism, slavery, war and morally grey decisions. Veilguard feels afraid to be uncomfortable. The companions so far don't feel like people shaped by a harsh world. They feel like upbeat characters written to be agreeable, quirky and easy to digest. It makes the whole thing feel tonally wrong.

The gameplay has also been simplified to the point where it barely resembles the older games. Tactical combat has been replaced with a button-mashing action system, party control is reduced, and positioning matters far less. Exploration is mostly linear, with corridor-like maps and obvious dead ends that usually reward you with a few coins or vendor junk.

Even the RPG systems feel shallow. After several hours I finally found a merchant, only to discover that the shop is locked behind arbitrary shop levels, and the available items are mostly just upgrades of equipment I already had. Previous Dragon Age games made shopping and looting feel meaningful. Here it feels stripped back and unrewarding.

Veilguard looks polished, but it doesn't feel like Dragon Age. It feels like a simplified action RPG with writing that is too childish for its own story.

If you are looking for Dragon Age Origins this is not the game. Zones are linear, combat is simplified and the most character are less then memorable. 

Dragon Age Origins - Awesome!
Dragon Age 2 - Hack and slash (can skip)
Dragon Age Inquisition - Bring the game back towards Origins but not 100%
Dragon Age The Veilguard - SLOP... Traaaaash... Character Taash know the word nonbinary but is illiterate.

I gave this game a chance after staying away from it due to the reviews. After a while, I figured perhaps the reviewers were exaggerating some stuff, and even if the game has bad narrative and puzzles then at least it could be stupid fun. I thought the combat looked flashy and the characters beautiful, I don't care that they "disneyfied" them, and I told myself that perhaps a game that tries to be softer on the senses can be a nice break from all the noise.

I did love the character creator, it has a ton of options, you can even give your character vitiligo which makes for a unique look.

However, while I can look past the forced inclusivity as it's whatever to me, a bad story if the gameplay is good, and repetitive gameplay if it hooks me (I love Tetris for example), this game does have some glaring issues that do make the rest more annoying.

First of all, it's mostly combat, and after you get past the flashiness of it, it's mostly button mashing with some action-breaking options. The puzzles are indeed insulting, besides being super simple, you don't even get a moment to think because your companions are like, "oh look, a switch up there" the instant you enter the area. The areas are corridors you follow from start to finish, mostly fighting and doing the aforementioned puzzles, with some uninspired pickups along the way (stuff like gold, materials, and some marginally improved gear). I can't see how this game would have any replay value.

Then, since the game is not that engaging it does make me notice the problems with the writing, it's awful. In nearly every conversation someone is saying something nice about someone else, patting each other on the back, saying platitudes, repeating stuff that has been said recently. I entered a room to place some items I didn't even know I had because my character was born with them, and after placing each item she told the story behind it, it was mostly disconnected from anything I've done, trying to establish a back…

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the character creator offers extensive customization options.

citations.review_text:
I'm not through playing yet, but from where I am in the game, I've really enjoyed it. The graphics are great. I've had no problems with the mechanics. I actually haven't played any other Dragon Age game before so I really don't have anything to base it off of there besides other RPGs and I think it sits up there with the mid tier ones pretty well. I enjoyed the character creation part. You can really tweak just about anything you want to. I have enjoyed most of the characters so far. And I can see that a lot of the negative reviews are from people who have played other Dragon Age games. And I can say that as someone who has not played any of the others, I really do like it. I got it to fill the void that was left by finishing a third round of Baldur's Gate and not wanting to start another right away and it's done the trick so far. 
If you like a good RPG, I say give this a try even if you haven't played the other Dragon Age games, you don't need to in order to enjoy this game.
8/10 from me so far!

claims.claim: Reviewers state that character appearance customization is limited, noting restrictions on body shape options.

citations.review_text:
i think it's a very fun game. i am currently playing a Qunari rogue, and i got to the point of meeting the veil jumpers. i unfortunately had to stop playing for the day after getting through a fight with Neve and one of the veil jumpers by my side because my mouse kept disconnecting during the fight.

overall, i would rate the game pretty highly so far. i wish i could do more to customize my character's physical appearance - body, not face - but i am still enjoying the game and don't mind the limited body customization

Origins is dated and janky, but still good by modern standards. DA2 was obviously low-budget, but felt fine. DAI was and is incredible.

DA:O was intended for 17-year olds. DA: Veilguard was released in 2024, which means the average player who was interested in Dragon Age is hovering over ~30 years old. Despite this it feels like I'm playing a game targeted at 8-year olds. 

The Veilguard feels like someone made a mod for Fortnite and then hired a bunch of second-screen writers. Every relevant piece of information is repeated 15 times, and characters feel more like caricatures that feel faker than a cardboard cutout.

Mechanically speaking the combat feels smooth, but companions are no longer meaningful contributors and customization has dropped down to practically nil. 

This results in a game that manages to look both better and worse than DAI with worse writing than any of the games that came before targeted at an entirely new player base.

If you're like me and you want to know how it ends then go for it, but I cannot otherwise recommend buying this game. This doesn't feel like Dragon Age at all. You'd be better off watching a youtube summary.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as action-oriented and smooth, featuring options for dodging and parrying.

citations.review_text:
An excellent game ABSOLUTELY tarnished by people's expectations.

----

So, bear with me here. I'm not gonna spend ages making this a masterpiece of a review.

I honestly do not get the hate this game gets. Is it as good as the previous dragon ages? I don't know. But as someone whom has played the entire series: combat is satisfying and intuitive. You have a ton of combos and weapon types to play around with. And although it's different from previous games, taking on a much more hack-n-slash or souls-like intuitive, it's still incredibly fun. Story is engaging (albiet not as strong as the previous games), and the exploration and quests are still a heavy focus.

-Is the writing as good as the previous Dragon Age games?
NO. But it's no where as near bad as some of the comments make it out to be. Still dark and engaging. Like, one of the first things you come across is a horror-esque scene of an entire village, which has been pretty much, for lack of spoilers, been turned into something out of Resident Evil. There's also that classic Bioware charm where it feels like half of your decisions will be remembered by at least someone.

As per another incredibly popular review, claiming that the "game is monotonous" and the combat boils down to "button mashing," I honestly wonder if they were playing on the lowest difficulty. Because let me tell you, this is honestly the hardest game in the series in terms of combat at normal difficulty. You will die unless you learn how to dodge or parry.

-Is it different from the other games in the series?
Yes. But I certainly would not call it bad. It still feels like it takes place right within the universe, just from the perspective of a totally different character from the first 3 games. I honestly think that the heavy politics of Inquisition ruined what people remembered from its roots: Dark at times, story-driven fantasy, with satisfying combat. And for that, it's not much different.

...Although I cannot hesitate eno…

this is yet another example of a game that got a bad rep after a few negative reviews. obviously everyone is entitled to their own opinions and a lot of the criticism is completely valid. however, these days, it feels like a lot of people are looking for any reason not to enjoy a game. I held off playing the veilguard for so long because of it. 


I'm early game, but thus far I have found many aspects enjoyable. here's a few:

GRAPHICS: some find the art style to be cartoonish, I can definitely see that, but I actually quite like it. they didn't hold back on the details, either. in cut scenes even the tongues move realistically as they speak and the hair moves so fluidly as well. the landscapes are stunning even on lower graphic settings. 

COMBAT: it's smooth, very customisable and they did a great job at having it reflect the characters class too. the controls have been taking a bit of getting used to but I ended up just changing the key bindings. I also much prefer the 'tab' abilities to command team members as opposed to previous games' methods.

ACCESSABILITY: there's a lot of really great settings that allow you to tailor things like combat as I mentioned earlier. you can change things individually such as enemy damage, reactiveness, difficulty etc. I was grateful for the ability to lower the response time for blocking attacks because I'm a button masher and sometimes it takes the game a hot minute to register I'm trying to defend after clicking LMB relentlessly lmao. you can change the settings any time too. 

CHARACTER CUSTOMISATION: hooooooly hell there's so much to customise. I will say, it's not the most impressive character creation I've seen but it is in no way lacking. I really like how you can change your appearance in game as well with no extra cost. they are really accommodating in this way, you can change your skills around at any point too. I also really enjoyed choosing my backstory. the options were pretty unique, usually I go with rogue + assas…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the combat system relies heavily on repetitive button mashing and simple attack spamming rather than deep strategy.

citations.review_text:
There is so much I could say about this game, but the simplest thing I can say to convey what this game is like is to say that it is the most "Aggressively Okay" game I've ever played. It does nothing well, nothing, the writing is a joke, the characters are bland and safe, the story is a mistake, the lore, while at times interesting, is completely out of place with the world of Dragon Age, and the gameplay? The Gameplay that everyone says "Well, at least the gameplay was good?" That gameplay? It's the worst part of the game. It's tedious, boring, repetitive, uninteresting, and basically is just boiled down to button mashing until a fight is over. It's not hard at all, not remotely, and you don't need to even Think to get through a single fight. It's just spam light attack or heavy attack, until you level up enough to unlock spamming light attack 3 times and Then heavy attack 1-2 times. That's it, that's all you get, other than holding an attack button for a guard break attack. Heck, most of the options you unlock are basically useless, or far too situational to be helpful. 

Look, tldr, if you liked Any Dragon Age game, even Dragon Age 2, you'll hate this one. If you've never played a Dragon Age game but have played basically Any other RPG or action game, you'll hate this game. If this is your first game you've ever played, Maybe you'll like it, until you play Anything else and realize that this game is not worth your time even remembering.

Aaaa i dont really know how to say this other then as plainly as i can.
I bought the game on discount, went in with an open mind as one can.
Sure they scrambled the lore to make it work
The whole LGBTQ thing is annoying mainly cause - sure add a non-binary character if you wish but at least make it good. Taash i wanted to punch in the face first 5 minutes after i had been forced to recruite her. She is simply a whiny selfinsert of someone who thinks the patriarchy is the biggest threat to the universe. The character is written poorly, Extremely poorly. Her entire personality is that she is a ♥♥♥♥♥ and  they/them and then get pissy about everything else around her.
Then u got the vegan necromancer. Like.. what?
But if that wasnt realistic enough then u got the italian assassin who doesnt ever ♥♥♥♥♥♥ flirt himself but apparently my main character pulling 0 charisma oneliners back to back and getting a "aha ok" level of response is a "relationship" according to the game.
Bioware used to be known for the RPG stuff, companions, story, all of it. 
It feels like Dragon Age from Temu.
Replay value : zero
Combat : fun for the first 15 hours then it gets repetative. Only thing keeping bosses alive for longer than 10 seconds is their stupid immunity mechanics.
Lore: forgiveable at least they tried
Writing: absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

Play the game through once if you are a fan of the series just to tie it off, but dont buy it unless its on 75%.

Mainly it just pisses me off that they butchered a good thing and then bought reviews to try to pretend its not ♥♥♥♥. U cant piss in a bowl and pretend its soup.

5/10

Yes, it's hammier than a can of Spam.
Yes, it's cheesier than a cheesy thing.
Yes, combat boils down to dodge roll and hope you don't get stun locked.
But it's still  a fun high fantasy romp around with enough call backs be try to stich together a coherant story.

Yes, it's not subtle with it's politically correct in-your-face-hand-wringing-wokeness. But that kind of boils down to me getting annoyed at the whinging tone of an otherwise strong character and two lines of forced plural nouns that left my 50+ YO brain trying to figure out who the object of the sentence was.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the character creation tool as robust, featuring detailed sliders and comprehensive options for customization.

citations.review_text:
This one I went in to with very low expectations but ended up enjoying quite a lot. It's a game most clearly cut from the Mass Effect 2/3 mold and delivers that classic Bioware presentation in spades. The gameplay flows very well and that is what kept me hooked throughout my play through. It also features a very robust character creator - the face morpher is a great idea for designing a base look - and is shrewdly used as the demo, indeed, it was the itch to see my characters in context that finally got me to shell out for a month of EA Play. On top of that you have instant access to character modification, transmog, and a plethora of other welcome quality-of-life features.

Where Bioware has dropped the ball massively is in the writing department. Every single hint of a sharp edge in the dialogue, characterisation, etc., has been sanded down to such a degree that the whole thing winds up as 'my first RPG' for the MCU generation. As many have said before, there must have been a permanent HR representative in the writer's room. I expected this and went in with the aim of going as Renegade as possible, but it's just not an option, only varying degrees of milquetoast. However, this, rather perversely, freed me up from having to give a crap about the stories and characters and just get down to enjoying the exploration, gameplay, and other assorted Bioware vibes it delivers. So, yes, a massive caveat here, but still a worthwhile bit of offensively inoffensive fun to be had.

It kills me to do this. It does. I have played and loved the Dragon Age series since DA:O came out. I played that game months after it came out and it blew me away to the point where it is my Favorite Game OF ALL TIME! If I could play one more videogame before I died, it would be DA:O. I have a Dragon Age tattoo. I have played the first three games so many times that, collectively, I probably have over two thousand hours in them. But Dragon Age: the Veilguard? Yeah, I can't recommend this.

Let me put it this way: I would play this game in quick bursts. 2-3 hours at the most was what I could stomach. Then, IMMEDIATELY AFTER I quit, I would boot up Skyrim and play for twice as long. I played both games literally in tandem. And now that I think about it, that's the most telling, damning thing I can say about this game. That both games are supposed to be RPGs and one (the most modern) failed so spectacularly at its job that I had to go to the other -- considered one of the BEST RPGs of all time and an absolute dinosaur -- as a kind of palate cleanser. If that doesn't tell you what this game is like, I don't know what will. I don't know how else to explain it. 

Its a beautiful game. It is. I love the character creation. The fact that I get hands down my favorite character creation in any videogame (outside of the Sims) in one of the worst I've ever played is so damn depressing to me (the body customization itself could have been more in-depth but that's neither here nor there). I liked some of the companions (I would raze entire cities to the ground for Manfred and Assan), hated others, and felt meh about the rest. The romances (of which DA USED to be famous for) were shallow and unimpressive and clearly written by people who have never experienced passion or romance in their entire lives. And the choices? What choices? None of them were well-written and none had any effect on the plot except for the barest of bones. They completely retconned so much of the previous tr…

I held off from playing this game in fear it wouldn't be on par with the previous DA games. I should have hopped on sooner lol. First off, the character creation is such a huge upgrade from DA Inquisition. It's very similar to the Baldur's Gate 3 character creation except DA Veilguard does an exceptional job by giving you sliders to customize to your hearts content. Rook looks amazing in the cutscenes and the graphics are phenomenal. I enjoy the combat system and love how fluid it feels. I added a couple of mods to heighten my experience with the game (I highly recommend going on Nexus Mods). It made my experience with the game 100x better! There are so many missions to do and and the storyline is great and immersive. Please give this game a try and don't mind the negative reviews. I didn't think I would enjoy the game but I'm 33 hours deep into it and only had the game for a week. For anyone that has played Inquisition and the previous games, there are so many cameos and references to give that bit of nostalgia :)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game world features stunning visuals, gorgeous environments, and high graphical fidelity.

citations.review_text: This game is so fun from the combats, character customization and the beautiful visuals. My only problem with the game is that this game requires powerful pc. I only have a midrange pc so sometimes the game crash but weirldly it happens at almost the end of the game. Overall i rate this game 10/10, you dont have to play previous game so for the newcomers you can just go ahead and play this game instead of play the prequals first.

I've had a lot of fun playing this game.  Visuals are amazing - as has been echoed by both the positive and negative reviews, environments are truly gorgeous.  Combat is fun - I just finished Nioh 3 and the combat here was a nice change of pace (obviously, this game's combat is not anywhere near as mechanically demanding as something like Nioh 3).  Voice acting / writing is a bit much in places.  I've played the other Dragon Age games and enjoyed this one - but I was just looking for a fun game and not necessarily something that was strictly in line with the other Dragon Age games.  

My only words of advice are don't play as a mage at first, choose rogue or fighter. I normally choose mage type characters but after reading several reviews about classes, I went with fighter at first and I am glad I did.  I eventually started a mage on the PS5 version (via PS Plus) and I have enjoyed it but I can see where it would have been frustrating as a first character without any experience with the game.

Solas is an interesting character. Game looks beautiful.

Gameplay is repetitive and bland. Gear and skills barely matter. Story wildly swings between trying to be serious and doing MCU quirk chungus dialogue. The result sucks.

I want to love this game. I love Dragon age. It runs smooth, the graphics are nice. The writing so bad, and everyone is joking every 2 second like superhero films. Rooks personality is already decided it feels like. At 30 hours of playing, the story gets better. At 36 hours, it is the dialouge, and how my rook has a awful personality. Its very cringey. The game feels like a tutorial the whole time. There is time for lighthearted moments, but the world is ending, I shouldn't be having cheesy convos every 2 seconds. It feels like scooby doo, but bad. 50 HOUR UPDATE: The companions of the game are just written bad. Taash being Trans is great. I love that. Zevhran was my boy in Origins and I loved him for being Bi, who he was. Taash being a insufferable little ♥♥♥♥ is the problem. Each companion trying to have some quick witted remark like in marvel movies is so bizare and misplace in this series. It is very evident that the 3 games that this was going to be was just pushed together in the end. It is devastating to play it longer and it feel worse. In summary it feels like a phone game in the world of Dragon Age. its very limited. Inquistion was way better and headed in as good directions I don't know how we ended up with whatever this game is. After so many of the OG people left and the direction of the story changed 3 times (I think) It feels like EA just had Bioware release it so they could do mass effect. The last few years of dragon age (15 years) they have wanted to make a live service game. I hope they never do. Dragon Age doesn't need to be live service. This was my favorite lore and storytelling series. Its now something different. 3/10.

Game is worth it.

About what i expected. The goofy party characters were too woke, but at least well voice acted. The game looks and runs great. Pacing is good and the story is fine. However, it doesn't feel like a Dragon Age.  The modular areas were all nice, but felt disconnected. Ultimately, it kept me busy, but i'm glad i waited for a deep discount. Shame to see bioware fumble what should have been a much better game...

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the combat system is fun, featuring action-oriented mechanics and engaging class playstyles.

citations.review_text:
Bought the game specifically because of all the whining about queer characters. Very soon after bought the deluxe upgrade. The game is gorgeous, combat is a good time even for someone who is more used to turn-based, and if you're in it for the story and characters, very replayable! I think I'm on playthrough... 4? The party is fun, though some of their companion sidequests can get a little repetitive or tedious (as is the nature of sidequests). Banter is good enough I almost never fast-travel just to trigger more of them.

My mage got to stab people with a mageknife all playthrough. Very good. Give mages pointy things.

The character creator is out of this world and I've spent something like another 10 hours in the separate "game" download just making people. A+ choice to release the creator separately and make those characters import-able for when you finally get around to the playthrough for that ONE specific character.

Edit: oh! also played one round on steam deck. didn't run in to any problems at all, but it definitely did a disservice to the graphics, they deserve a big beautiful monitor.

I waited a long time for this game, did it meet all expectations of former Dragon Age fans? No, but is it still a fun game with amazing graphics and one of the best Dragfon Age fighting systems I played? Yes. Would recommend this to new and old Dragon Age fans who are just looking for a fun time in a Fantasy game.

This review is two years late, but I enjoyed it. Like all of the DA entries it has good moments and not so good moments and a few awful ones. This is a series I play for the lore and worldbuilding. I went in wanting lore questions answered after 10 years and for the most part I received the answers I hoped for. The environments are beautiful, the music is memorable, and it runs extremely well on both my gaming computer and my Steam deck. Also, I really appreciated the combat modernization and am thankful I don't have to play another RTWP slog where I'm dreading battles to get to cutscenes. I've beaten the original BG games oodles of times and Pillars of Eternity and all the past DA games. I've served my RTWP time lol. Sometimes I just want to push the sword button and do sword things.

The level designs are thoughtful and I felt rewarded for exploring off the path. The game is very tight and polished. Really fun to play.

The art style isn't that much of a departure to me with the exception of a few characters and locations. Most of the environments just look like more painterly versions of Inquisition's, and the overly shiny character graphics are fixed  (everyone looked like a salamander in that game, I'm sorry!) A few characters were a bit overtuned and as a result, stood out in a "we invaded your IP" way. I get it - it's art, but that was my interpretation of it.

You can tell it went through development hell on the writing. Every line of dialogue feels first draft or spliced from voiceover or scripts and as a result you get a lot of repetition, weird out of context moments (people repeating the same names over and over as though they're the first one to say them), and what comes across as not having faith that the player will grasp the setting.

Rook is unfortunately my least favorite protagonist of Dragon Age and I mean this in the most constructive way I can. Huge thanks to the DA Community Council for pushing back on V1 of Rook, who I understand was much wor…

It's not perfect by a long shot, but it turned out remarkably well despite EA's meddling. Yes, it's different from the first three (which also had their differences). It's ok to let them be different. Great visual and sound design, overall entertaining story, fun and wonderfully voiced characters that I got quite attached to (with one twist that really took me by surprise), and a satisfying ending. I did miss the old RTWP combat system a bit, but still enjoyed the action-oriented system adapted from Mass Effect.

Overall the game is fantastic. A VERY solid combat system that makes use of every button of the controller  with well designed intent. Nothing ever feels out of place, and although you have to periodically keep an eye on your cooldowns, it's never more than a fraction of a second. Nor is the GUI invasive into what you need to be paying attention to while you're fighting. It has a solid arcadey hack and slash feel to it. Nothing too deep, but developed enough to be engaging throughout the battles. The enemy health is also well balanced for the most part. (Granted how much damage you do is entirely in the hands of how the player wants to play, which is another merit)  The story is pretty solid as well. A lot of engaging side story that although aren't as syndicating in complexity, as something like Yakuza they're still entertaining enough to want to get to know more of the interactions between the characters. This is definitely a game worthy of the name BioWare (♥♥♥♥ EA though) 
I literally started another campaign immediately after I cleared it for the first time. S-tier product.

The core gameplay loop is admittedly a lot of fun, which is why I have almost 200 hours and counting sunk into this thing.  The character creator is also one of the best I've ever seen (real hair physics!  tons of options!)  But good God is this a terrible Dragon Age game.  Everything has been sanitized and polished up to try and make this a cozy, feel-good game, at the expense of ignoring previously established lore.  And the new lore additions are frankly garbage.  And what used to be a complex, morally grey setting now has clearly delineated Good Guys and Bad Guys.  Good Guys are Good no matter who they are or what horrors they've been stated to have done in previous games (like the Antivan Crows going from a group that uses child slavery to get new assassins to being noble freedom fighters) and Bad Guys are Bad with no further reasoning behind why they do the things they do.  They're just Evil(TM).  (also, anyone who dares question the protagonist is automatically Bad)

This game gets a lot of hate, and it is not all warranted. Is it the fourth Dragon Age game that we hoped for? Absolutely not. Maybe I'm biased because I want to linger over long in a world that has meant so much to me for so long. But the fighting mechanics are awesome, the graphics are INSANELY good, the character creator is PEAK (no more AWFUL hairstyles!). Are there plot holes? Yup. Storylines that didn't get flushed out as much as they should have or deserved? Yup. But Emmrich Volkarin alone makes the game worth it, come on. Enjoy it for what it is and what we got, not what we thought we deserved or what we wanted.

dragon age is the franchise that got me into gaming, and it kind of devastates me that this is going to end up being the last one. it's a gorgeous game with some of the best combat in the series, and there are so many areas of the game that are just powerhouse areas--like the seige on weisshaupt--that should go down as some of the best set pieces in the series. the character creator is mind-blowing and some of the choices you can make to build up your character--including being able to toy with your character's gender and sexuality in ways that effect dialogue--are super cool. i loved seeing characters pop up from the dragon age books, comics, and shows (especially my little grey wardens), and i love the relationships you can build with your companions and the ways your investment in them can effect outcomes later in the game.

the tragedy of this game is all of the meddling behind the scenes that led to the writers not having enough time to flesh out the things that they wanted to. swapping from a multiplayer game to single player and having to rebuild so much of the story in a short turnaround was a knife to the throat here. there are things that come off as clunky that you can tell they just did not have enough time to expand on in the way that they wanted to--especially with characters like taash. beautiful, important concepts that just did not get the space to breathe that they needed. 

this game also unfortunately nukes the lore of the rest of the franchise in a way that has soured my ability to replay the older games. what is the point of struggling with saving thedas if you know that when it comes down to it, by the end of the fourth game, it will be gone no matter what you do?

i'm still putting this as a recommendation because i think that if you're playing this as just a game on its own, it is a deeply entertaining and fun experience. but as a franchise installment (and ultimately a series ender) it is a pretty bummer note to end on.

This is true modern slop!
Some lore and story reveals were good, but are not worth playing for.
Just read a synopsis somewhere, the game is boring.
Choices don't matter and it's too easy even at nightmare difficulty. Puzzles stink too.
Sad very sad

I spent a lot of hours on this game trying to be a completionist, but I found myself most of the time cringing at the terrible dialogue, atrocious writing, and inexplicable design choices of this game. The reviews that call it a good game but not a good Dragon Age game were actually understating it. It's not even a good game at all. It's not even a good piece of fiction in particular.

The only positive thing I can say for this game is that this game looks beautiful. The environments are drop-dead gorgeous, but then your companions' banter ruins it all. If you're expecting DA:O Alistair-level of banter here, you'd be sorely disappointed.

Also, achievement bugs—as of this writing I'm sitting at 94%, which should have been 100% by now in one playthrough but it's bugged as hell. It remains to be seen whether I complete it, but when I remember what a slog it all was...

None of your companions are remotely even likeable. The only character that I like here isn't even a companion (it's Manfred). The anachronistic writing, such as using the terms gender and non-binary, are off-putting, and I consider myself progressive. The Qunari have become a caricature, the Elves have suddenly lost depth, the Dwarves are almost absent, and the one-dimensional Saturday morning cartoon villains don't help.

Buy this at a deep discount (or if it's free in a bundle), but it's safe to say that Veilguard killed Dragon Age. The secret ending is literally just Marvel slop. Stay away.

Rook is unfortunately my least favorite protagonist of Dragon Age and I mean this in the most constructive way I can. Huge thanks to the DA Community Council for pushing back on V1 of Rook, who I understand was much wor…

To say I’m a Dragon Age fan doesn’t quite do it justice. With over 800 hours of playtime across all four games (I’ll be honest, the second one is at the bottom of my list), I feel qualified to write a review:
If you’re expecting a classic sequel to Inquisition, you’re in the wrong place. As Varric already said in the 2020 cinematic trailer, it’s time for a new hero. No magic hand, no ancient prophecy.
Consequently, Veilguard feels quite detached from the entire Dragon Age lore, which, with Origins, still introduced you with awe to the lore surrounding the Dark Spawn. 
With that in mind, I think it’s a solid game! The world is incredibly beautiful, and there are glimpses into places that were previously only mentioned by name. 
The decisions regarding the companions feel rather black-and-white, especially toward the end, which is a real shame, since as a player you do make an effort to get to know the different characters and wrap up their stories. 
I also find that it takes a while to warm up to the characters beyond the usual party banter. At this point, it’s important to mention that Manfred is the best.  The variety in the skill system really drew me in, and of course the outfits, heh! 
All in all, for me, the combat, the nostalgia, and the beautiful scenery outweigh the rest, so I think it’s absolutely solid.
(please don’t come for my kneecaps)

i'm a card carrying member of the tumblr crew, with dyed hair and pronouns and everything, and i found this game intolerable. beautiful scenery and character creation, stupid plot, stupid characters, just a waste of time and money.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that previous choices from earlier games in the franchise do not carry over or matter.

citations.review_text: I had a lot of fun with this game. There were certainly things that were disappointing; mostly being that so very few previous choices in the series mattered. Really just felt like things revolving around the inquisitor and Solas mattered. A small moment of that being in a conversation with the inquisitor; love interests only get brought up if the inquisitor dated Solas. Just adding a line for each romance would have been nice. Like especially since one of the other romances from DAI is in this game and Rook meets him. I will play this again, and I love several of the characters. I just wish more had mattered from before.

So, this game is Great for what it is. 

It's pretty well known that Bioware and the Dragonage team really struggled witht he production of this game. Mainly because of the awful Trend amoung companies to cling to the Live Service Game fad. Which 1000% awful from the go. 

In spite of being told Several times to change the game frame work, to Live Service to Single Player RPG, To Live Service again and some how settling between the 2.  I will admit that this game is a Ginormous failure, It undersold and is not what fans were expecting. 

Here's where the game excel's. 
Game play is fluid, the Story is coheesive and enjoyable it's a otherwise Good AAA Fantasy Action RPG with I felt Solid Representation

Here's where it fails
Your choices from previous games were discarded. this was a cornerstone of why DragonAge games did well, the world felt living and breathing and as a result infintley more engaging. The lingering liveservice elements stink,and it lacks replayability unless you are obssessed like yours truly.

That said in the end I really enjoyed it.

Is it the best Dragon Age? No. Was it rushed? Yeah. But it gave us an ending to Sola's story and doesn't deserve to get as much hate as it does but that's just me. The romance and character's are done very well and it was visually really pleasing. The lack of past game consequences was disappointing but at least BioWare didn't abandon DA. I'm more in love with the companions than the storyline and maybe I only recommend it because of how much I love the old games but you should at least play it once. Though I recommend waiting till this game is on sale, do NOT buy it full price.

For a Dragon Age game? It's underwhelming, to be totally honest. 

Rook is such a flat and uninspiring character, and since they are the character you play as, it's just a bit of a slog. It feels like Rook is destined to be a sort of standard Hero archetype no matter what you do. The charm of the older Dragon Age games that allows you to play a nuanced character feels lost in this one. Very few of the decisions or dialog options feel like they really matter. The decisions you made in past games feel even less relevant. The combat is okay, but feels very button-mashy after a while. If you are a diehard Dragon Age fan, it might be worth it for the lore, but I honestly can't see myself playing it again.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that dialogue and companion writing feel simplistic, repetitive, or juvenile.

citations.review_text:
I spent a lot of hours on this game trying to be a completionist, but I found myself most of the time cringing at the terrible dialogue, atrocious writing, and inexplicable design choices of this game. The reviews that call it a good game but not a good Dragon Age game were actually understating it. It's not even a good game at all. It's not even a good piece of fiction in particular.

The only positive thing I can say for this game is that this game looks beautiful. The environments are drop-dead gorgeous, but then your companions' banter ruins it all. If you're expecting DA:O Alistair-level of banter here, you'd be sorely disappointed.

Also, achievement bugs—as of this writing I'm sitting at 94%, which should have been 100% by now in one playthrough but it's bugged as hell. It remains to be seen whether I complete it, but when I remember what a slog it all was...

None of your companions are remotely even likeable. The only character that I like here isn't even a companion (it's Manfred). The anachronistic writing, such as using the terms gender and non-binary, are off-putting, and I consider myself progressive. The Qunari have become a caricature, the Elves have suddenly lost depth, the Dwarves are almost absent, and the one-dimensional Saturday morning cartoon villains don't help.

Buy this at a deep discount (or if it's free in a bundle), but it's safe to say that Veilguard killed Dragon Age. The secret ending is literally just Marvel slop. Stay away.

If it had simply been called The Veilguard, I probably wouldn't have been so disappointed. But as a huge fan of Dragon Age: Origins (which is literally a masterpiece to me, one of the greatest RPGs ever made), Dragon Age: The Veilguard ended up being a very hollow experience.

It has strayed so far from the original dark medieval fantasy RPG that it has become almost unrecognizable.

Things I didn't enjoy:

Before anything else, this game was originally designed as a live-service title (Thanks to EA for ruining every Dragon Age game after Origins with some kind of BS). Even though they eventually abandoned that idea during development, many of its systems still feel like they were built around it: the loot system, progression, inventory, factions, combat, and more. I'm not a fan of that design philosophy at all.

1. The writing is underwhelming. The story is weak, the lore is butchered, and the dialogue is overly simple - often childish. There is an excessive overuse of words like "okay," "maybe," and "well," making conversations feel repetitive and primitive. The overall tone is lighthearted and juvenile, as if you're watching a Marvel movie rather than playing a Dragon Age game.

2. The puzzles are surprisingly simplistic. Most of them require almost no thought, which makes them feel more like filler than actual gameplay.

3. The art style leans heavily toward a cartoony, Disney-like aesthetic, reminding me more of games like Fortnite or Overwatch than Dragon Age.

4. The combat is flashy and repetitive. Once again, it feels designed for fans of Marvel-style action games (such as Guardians of the Galaxy) or more casual action RPGs like Hogwarts Legacy, rather than for players looking for the tactical depth that Dragon Age was once known for.

5. The soundtrack is decent, but nothing more. It's cinematic, polished, and clearly expensive, yet somehow forgettable and hollow. It reminds me of the music in many modern blockbuster movies - you hear it once and never thi…
